newsitem.title: USA: South Korea to buy U.S. "Stinger" Missiles.
newsitem.headline: South Korea to buy U.S. "Stinger" Missiles.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday it planned to sell 1,065 shoulder-fired "Stinger" anti-aircraft missiles and 213 launchers to South Korea for $307 million.
The Pentagon notified Congress that Seoul had requested the Stingers for defense against any attack from North Korea. It would be the first such transfer of the sophisticated weapons to South Korea.

The missiles, which can be fired by a single soldier with the launcher resting on a shoulder, find and track their targets after launch. They are made by the Hughes Missiles System Co., a division of General Motors Corp..

"This is the first sale of "Stinger" missiles to Korea and it will enable the Korean Army to develop a defense capability with an ability to protect itself from unwarranted aggressi0on from the air as well as enhance its interoperability with U.S. forces," the Pentagon said in an announcement.
Such major foreign military sales require approval by Congress but the sale is expected to be completed without opposition.

The United States and South Korea are close allies, but there has been recent tension between their defense departments over the possibility that South Korea might buy heavy Russian-made SA-12 anti-aircraft missiles. Defense Secretary William Cohen has instead urged Seoul to buy U.S.-built Patriot anti-aircraft missiles.
